title: Book 3 — Thalia, Chapter 439
paragraphs: But on the fifth or sixth day after these things, the following happened to him. A fisherman, having caught a large and beautiful fish, thought it should be given as a gift to Polycrates. He accordingly brought it to the door of the palace and said that he wished to come into the presence of Polycrates, and when he had obtained this, he gave him the fish, saying: “O king, having caught this fish, I did not think fit to bring it to the market, although I am one who lives by the labor of his hands; but it seemed to me worthy of you and your kingship: therefore I bring it and present it to you.” He, pleased at the words spoken, answered thus: “You have done exceedingly well, and double thanks are due to you — for your words and also for your gift; and we invite you to come to dinner.” The fisherman, thinking this a great thing, went away to his house; and the servants, as they were cutting up the fish, found in its belly the signet-ring of Polycrates. As soon as they had seen it and taken it up, they carried it rejoicing to Polycrates, and giving him the signet-ring, they told him how it had been found. Perceiving that the matter was of God, he wrote upon paper all he had done and all that had happened to him, and having written, he dispatched it to Egypt.
